title: Volition
summary: The primary choice to focus or not, and volition as axiomatic. This ladder places it after the metaphysically given.

lessons.title: The primary choice
lessons.objective: Name the primary act of volition: the choice to focus the mind or not to focus it.

exercises.prompt: What is the primary choice?

choices.text: To focus the mind or not to focus it
To pick a career before any mental effort
To feel whatever emotion arrives first
To wait until other people decide for you

feedback.note: Volition starts with one choice: raise the mind to focus, or leave it unfocused. Later choices depend on that one.

exercises.prompt: Which pair names the two sides of that primary choice?

choices.text: Focus, or not
True, or false
Good, or bad
Public, or private

feedback.note: The primary alternative is focus or the failure to focus. Truth and value come later, after the mind is in use.

exercises.prompt: Match each label to what it names in this unit.

pairs.right: The effort to be fully aware

feedback.note: Focus is the effort of awareness. Choosing not to make that effort is the other side of the same primary choice.

exercises.prompt: Complete the statement of the primary choice.

feedback.note: The word for the primary act is focus. Wishing, voting, and drifting are not that act.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that states the primary choice.

feedback.note: State it in that order: the primary choice, the act of focus, and the alternative of not focusing.

exercises.prompt: If the mind is left drifting, what choice has been made?

choices.text: The choice not to focus
No choice at all, because drift is automatic
A choice made by the metaphysically given
A choice made by other people

feedback.note: Not focusing is still a side of the primary choice. It is not something the given facts do for you.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to whether it is the primary choice.

feedback.note: Words and feelings are not the first act. The first act is whether the mind is focused.

exercises.prompt: Name both sides.

feedback.note: Both sides belong to you: the effort of focus, and the choice not to make it.

exercises.prompt: Why is this choice called primary?

choices.text: Other mental work depends on whether you focus
It was the first idea in human history
It is the choice you announce in public
It is easier than any other choice

feedback.note: Primary means first in the order of choice. Thinking about a subject uses a mind that has been focused or not.

lessons.title: Focus before content
lessons.objective: Separate the effort of focus from later choices about what to think, say, or do.

exercises.prompt: What does the primary choice control directly?

choices.text: Whether you exert the effort of focus
Which facts exist in the world
How your eyes and ears rewrite what they sense
Events outside any human action

feedback.note: The direct object of the primary choice is your own mental effort, not the facts you will later identify.

exercises.prompt: A decision about what to say in an argument sits where, relative to focus?

choices.text: After the choice to focus or not
Before any choice to focus
In place of volition
Among the metaphysically given facts

feedback.note: Choosing a claim, a sentence, or an action is a further choice. It is not a substitute for focusing first.

exercises.prompt: Match each act to its place.

pairs.left: Raising the mind to full awareness

feedback.note: Content comes after effort. Dropping attention is the negative side of the same primary choice.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast.

feedback.note: You choose the effort. A conclusion is something a focused mind can then reach, not the effort itself.

exercises.prompt: Build the order this lesson teaches.

feedback.note: Effort of focus comes first. What you think, say, or do is chosen with a mind that is in focus or out of it.

exercises.prompt: Someone says volition means you can make any claim true by choosing it. What is wrong?

choices.text: It swaps a choice of content for the choice to focus
Nothing. Focus rewrites the facts
Volition covers only public speeches
There is no choice once a topic is named

feedback.note: Choosing to look does not choose what is there. The primary choice is the effort, not a decree about reality.

exercises.prompt: Match the mistake to the correction.

pairs.right: Focus is still the prior choice

pairs.left: I chose the fact into existence
pairs.right: Choice does not replace the given
The primary choice is mental effort

feedback.note: Feelings, facts, and wording are not substitutes for the effort of focus.

exercises.prompt: Fill the direct object of the primary choice.

feedback.note: Facts stay what they are. What you choose at the root is whether to exert the effort of looking at them.

exercises.prompt: Which item is a later choice, not the primary one?

choices.text: Which question to work on once you are focused
Whether to raise the mind to awareness
Whether to drop that effort
The choice to focus or not

feedback.note: A topic is content. You can take it up only because the primary choice about focus has a side.

lessons.title: Volition is axiomatic
lessons.objective: Explain why volition is axiomatic: an attempt to deny the choice already uses it.

exercises.prompt: In this unit, what does it mean to call volition axiomatic?

choices.text: You rely on the choice to focus in any attempt to deny it
A majority must approve it before it counts
It is true only when you feel free
It is an optional extra after all proof is finished

feedback.note: An axiom is in use in the act of questioning it. Denying volition still takes a mind that focuses on the denial.

exercises.prompt: Someone argues, at length, that no one can choose to think. What has that argument already done?

choices.text: Used the choice to focus on a claim
Shown that focus never happens
Turned volition into a metaphysically given rock
Avoided every act of awareness

feedback.note: A worked-out denial is evidence of focus, not a proof that focus was impossible.

exercises.prompt: Match each move to what it shows about volition.

feedback.note: The denial does not get outside the choice. Looking again is the choice in act.

exercises.prompt: Complete the axiomatic point.

feedback.note: The attempt itself is an act of focus. That is why volition is not a side claim you can set aside and then debate.

exercises.prompt: Build the reason volition is axiomatic.

feedback.note: The denier focuses in order to deny focus. The choice is in the attempt.

exercises.prompt: Which question still requires the choice to focus?

choices.text: Is volition real?
No question does, if the answer might be no
Only questions about food
Only questions asked after the axiom is proved from zero

feedback.note: Asking whether volition is real is already an exercise of the choice the question is about.

exercises.prompt: Match the status to the item.

pairs.left: The choice to focus or not

feedback.note: The axiom is the fact of that primary choice, not whichever conclusion a focused mind reaches.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two words this lesson pairs.

feedback.note: Axiomatic and focus belong together here: you cannot inspect the claim without the effort the claim is about.

exercises.prompt: What would a successful proof that nobody can focus have to avoid?

choices.text: Using focus to build the proof
Using paper
Using any grammar
Mentioning the metaphysically given

feedback.note: A proof is a focused effort. That effort is what a denial of volition cannot step outside of.

exercises.prompt: Where does this unit place the axiom of volition relative to the primary choice?

choices.text: The axiom is the fact of that choice to focus or not
The axiom is a different choice about politics
The axiom replaces focus with a feeling
The axiom says there is no primary choice

feedback.note: Volition as axiomatic does not add a second root. It names the same primary choice, which every denial still uses.

lessons.title: After the metaphysically given
lessons.objective: Place volition after the metaphysically given: what is given is not chosen, and choice is what can add man-made facts.

exercises.prompt: Why does this ladder teach volition after the metaphysically given?

choices.text: You need to know what is not chosen before you study what choice is
Volition comes first in the alphabet of units
The given is optional once choice exists
The given and the primary choice are the same fact

feedback.note: The given is the floor under volition. Choice does not vote on what had to be accepted as given.

exercises.prompt: Which item is metaphysically given, not a product of the choice to focus?

choices.text: That a thing is what it is
That you studied it today
The notes you chose to write
The effort you did or did not make

feedback.note: Identity is given. Study, notes, and effort are on the side of choice, which this unit takes up only after the given.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to the right side of the line.

pairs.left: A fact that is, apart from your choice
The choice to focus or not
A conclusion you reached by looking
pairs.right: Man-made by the use of choice

feedback.note: Keep the given on one side and volition on the other. What you learn by looking is man-made; the facts you look at are not.

exercises.prompt: Complete the placement.

feedback.note: The unit name for what is not up for choice is the metaphysically given. Volition is the next floor, not a rewrite of that one.

exercises.prompt: Build the order of the ladder at this point.

tokens.text: then the choice to focus or not

feedback.note: The given comes first on this ladder. The primary choice is what you study once that line is clear.

exercises.prompt: What can the choice to focus add?

choices.text: Man-made facts, such as knowledge you gain by looking
A new identity for things that already are
A world in which existence depends on a wish
The undoing of what is metaphysically given

feedback.note: Focus lets you know and act. It does not vote a new identity onto what is given.

exercises.prompt: Match the error to why it fails.

pairs.left: Choosing that A is not A
pairs.right: The given is not up for a vote

pairs.left: Skipping the given and starting at choice
pairs.right: This ladder puts volition after the given
Notes came from a choice to look

feedback.note: Do not move the given into the column of choice, and do not move your own products into the column of the given.

exercises.prompt: Fill the contrast.

feedback.note: Not chosen marks the given. Focus or not marks volition, which this unit places next.

exercises.prompt: Your decision to keep looking at a hard page is which kind of fact?

choices.text: A use of volition, not a metaphysically given fact
Metaphysically given, like identity
Neither, because reading is automatic
Both a vote on reality and a law of identity

feedback.note: Keeping your mind on the page is the primary choice in act. The page’s nature was already given.

lessons.title: Given, then the axiom
lessons.objective: Hold the unit in one order: the metaphysically given, the primary choice to focus or not, and volition as axiomatic.

exercises.prompt: Which order matches this unit?

choices.text: Metaphysically given, then focus or not, as an axiom
Axiom of politics, then feelings, then the given
Focus rewrites the given, then axioms are optional
Only the primary choice, with nothing given before it

feedback.note: Three points, one order: what is given, the primary choice, and that choice as axiomatic.

exercises.prompt: Match each point to its job in the unit.

pairs.right: What choice does not vote on
Denial of volition still uses it

feedback.note: Each label has one job. Do not trade them.

exercises.prompt: Build the unit in ladder order.

tokens.text: The primary choice is to focus or not

feedback.note: Read the three clauses in that order and you have the unit.

exercises.prompt: Which statement mixes the points incorrectly?

choices.text: Because volition is axiomatic, you can choose that A is not A
The given is not a product of focus
The primary choice is to focus or not
Denying volition uses the choice it denies

feedback.note: The axiom does not license a vote on the given. The other three statements are the unit itself.

exercises.prompt: Fill the three-point line.

parts.text: or not, and that fact is

feedback.note: Given, focus, axiomatic: the same three points, in the ladder’s order.

exercises.prompt: A student memorizes conclusions but never chooses to look. Which point did they miss?

choices.text: The primary choice is the effort of focus, not a stack of conclusions
They missed that conclusions are metaphysically given
They missed that axioms are settled by vote
They missed nothing; memory replaces focus

feedback.note: Conclusions are content. Without the choice to focus, the unit’s primary act has not been made.

exercises.prompt: Match the student move to the point it respects.

pairs.left: Refuses to treat identity as optional
Notices that a denial took effort

feedback.note: Each move lines up with one point of the unit. Together they are the whole lesson.

exercises.prompt: Complete the reminder.

feedback.note: Denial still focuses. That is the axiomatic point, kept after the given and after the name of the primary choice.

exercises.prompt: What is this unit’s whole claim, in one line?

choices.text: After the given, the primary choice to focus or not is axiomatic
Feelings discover facts, and the given is optional
Reality is whatever a group chooses
Volition replaces metaphysics

feedback.note: One line holds the ladder: the given stays unchosen, and the choice to focus or not is axiomatic.

exercises.prompt: Build the closing line.

feedback.note: Close on the unit summary: placement after the given, volition as axiomatic, and the primary choice to focus or not.
